_note: The [I] tier. Names, record fields and globals that a filter, a caller or a
neighbouring name produced and that nothing has yet checked. They are NOT symbols.
Nothing here is applied to Ghidra, nothing here is rendered into docs/symbols.md,
and nothing here may be cited as a finding. The corpus goes on calling these
FUN_... on purpose.
docs/symbols.json is the verified tier and its ratio is deliberately high - that
ratio is the only thing that makes it worth reading. A bulk pass over a subsystem
produces far more plausible names than checked ones, and pouring those in would
destroy the property that makes the file useful. So they land here instead.
Correction C3 in docs/decisions.md is what a coherent, unchecked model costs when
it is filed as fact.
PROMOTION IS A MOVE, NOT A COPY. Run a check that could have failed, add the
symbol to docs/symbols.json with that check written into its comment, and delete
the entry here in the same commit. An address that is verified in symbols.json
must NOT also appear in this file: a name in both is a name whose tier nobody can
read off. If the check goes the other way, DELETE the entry - do not soften it and
do not mark it partially confirmed, because a refuted hypothesis left on the page
is worse than one never written. The next reader cannot tell it from the ones
nobody has looked at yet.
Every entry carries a basis: the mechanical observation the guess rests on - an
L2.eng group and index, a widget-table membership, a shipped filename, a record
stride, a named caller. Not the reasoning; the SOURCE, so that when a basis turns
out to be unreliable everything resting on it can be found in one grep. An entry
whose basis is only "it is called from near something named" is the shape C3 took
and should be read as a question, not an answer.
The rate to expect is measured in docs/method.md section 7.3: the subject filter
runs 89% correct and the role hypothesis on top of it 58%. So roughly two in five
of the roles below are wrong, and the value of this file is that it says which two
in five to check first - not that it is right.
SCHEMA - confidence is an enum, ALWAYS one of three words, saying WHICH HALF of
the name a reader should distrust:
subject: what it is about is anchored to a string, an asset or a stride,
and the role word in the name may be wrong.
role:    the role is anchored (it is in a widget table, it is the painter a
dispatcher calls) and the subject is the guess.
both:    neither half has an independent anchor. A cluster of these that
touches no string and no shipped file is where C3 lives.
Three agents created this file on the same day and 29 of the 65 entries carried a
prose line in this key instead. Those were read and classified, and the prose they
held moved verbatim to caveat - what is anchored, what is not, and what would
refute it. Nothing was rewritten and nothing was discarded. An entry whose caveat
names no way of being wrong is not a hypothesis, it is a wish.
The enum is countable against the measured rates above. The caveat is not, and it
is not trying to be: several of the migrated entries turned out to have no doubt
about the NAME at all - the name is anchored on both halves and what is missing is
a save that exercises the field. That is a promotion note, not a confidence value,
and it is why there is no fourth word.
corrections holds claims in docs/symbols.json or in the documents that a pass
believes are WRONG but did not rewrite, because the entry belongs to another
subsystem or another agent is editing the same file. Each carries its evidence,
and each is a task for somebody rather than a resolved question.
See docs/method.md section 7.6.

functions.name: SendSupplies_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for screen 0x18, whose painter Screen_SendSupplies draws L2.eng group 33, 'Send supplies'.
functions.comment: The send-supplies overlay.

functions.name: Screen_MapInfo
functions.basis: The painter Screen_Draw dispatches for g_screenId 0x04, which Screen_FrameInput (0x0042FF10) sets after a map click that picked something. Branches to UnitPanel_Draw when a unit is picked and FUN_0041BEFE otherwise, on the same g_pickedTileFlags bits Map_Click uses.
functions.comment: docs/screens-county.md calls this 'the map information panel'; nothing has read what it draws.

functions.name: Merchant_SeasonTick
functions.comment: A season pass that does nothing. Called only from Season_Advance.
functions.basis: Position in Season_Advance's call list, between County_RecountMerchants and Army_RecountCountyTroops, and its address - it sits between Merchant_AdvanceAll (0x004280E9) and Merchant_ResetStall (0x0042847C) in the merchant neighbourhood.
functions.caveat: The body is eleven bytes and returns. So the name is a guess at what was removed, and it cannot be checked from this binary at all: an empty function has no evidence in it. Recorded because a reader of Season_Advance needs to know the slot is deliberately empty rather than missing, not because the name is worth anything.

functions.name: SaveLoad_Accept
functions.basis: Record 0 of g_saveLoadWidgets (0x004DDD78), frame 29 at (304, 64) - the yes of the yes/no pair whose no is the verified SaveLoad_Cancel; the two frames are a mailed hand thumb-up and thumb-down, not a tick and a cross. Its whole body is DAT_005CD41C = 100.
functions.comment: The save/load box's confirm button. What the sentinel 100 means to its reader has not been traced.

functions.name: SmackTest_Step
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the screen 0x44 widget table 0x004DDFA0, frames 68 and 66 at (208, 232) and (240, 232). Screen 0x44's painter draws L2.eng group 89, whose index 0 is 'Smack file testing'.
functions.comment: Pick the previous or next Smacker file on the developers' test screen.

functions.name: SmackTest_Close
functions.basis: Records 2 and 3 of 0x004DDFA0, frames 29 and 31 - the yes/no pair. It writes g_screenId.
functions.comment: Leave the Smacker test screen.

functions.name: Ratings_DrawPanel
functions.basis: Called by Screen_DrawWidgets for both 0x2E and 0x2F, the two Battle Master screens, and by Menu_NewGame before it opens its confirmation box.
functions.comment: Shared overlay for the two score screens. Being called from Menu_NewGame as well means the role may be wider than 'the ratings panel' - read it before promoting.

functions.name: Diplo_AdjustGift
functions.basis: Records 6 and 7 of g_diploWidgets, frames 68 and 66 at (184, 240) and (216, 240), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the minus/plus pair. The screen it sits on draws L2.eng group 72 index 18, 'Gift of', beside g_diploGold.
functions.comment: Raise or lower the offered gift; the hotspot id says which way.

functions.name: Diplo_PickLordCard
functions.basis: Screen_FrameInput calls it for g_screenId 0x0B immediately after Widget_Test over g_diploWidgets. It walks realms 1..5, skipping g_localPlayer and any realm with strength 0, and hit-tests FUN_004B1DEB(0x30, slot*100 + 0x31, 0x52, 0x4E) -- the same rectangle Diplo_DrawLordCard draws its inset in, with the same slot counter. On a hit it writes g_diploTarget and returns 1.
functions.comment: Selecting which rival the diplomacy screen is about. One reading of the body; the corroboration is that its rectangle is literally the painter's.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Close
functions.basis: Records 0 and 1 of the send-supplies widget table 0x004DD538: frames 29 and 31 at (320, 342) and (360, 346), hotspot ids 1 and 0 - the yes/no convention (frames 29 and 31 are a mailed hand thumb-up and thumb-down). It writes g_screenId twice.
functions.comment: Accept or cancel the supply shipment; the hotspot id says which.

functions.name: SendSupplies_Less
functions.basis: Records 2 and 4 of the same table, frame 27 at x 216, hotspot ids 0 and 2 - two rows of a pair whose other half is 0x0043B27A at frame 25.
functions.comment: Decrease the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: SendSupplies_More
functions.basis: Records 3 and 5 of the same table, frame 25 at x 296, hotspot ids 0 and 2.
functions.comment: Increase the amount of one commodity.

functions.name: Diplo_PickCountyFromMap
functions.basis: Screen_FrameInput calls it as FUN_0043B4CB(0x60, 0xB0) for g_screenId 0x1A, before the corner button. It returns 0 immediately when g_diploKind < 5 -- the five dialogs with no map on them -- and otherwise indexes g_minimapCounty at (mouseX - x) + (mouseY - y)*0x80 for a left press inside a 0x80 square, writing g_pickedCounty. A pixel whose county is 0 returns 0, i.e. not consumed.
functions.comment: The county picker on the ask-for-help and ask-for-attack dialogs. Diplo_DrawCountyRequest draws the same map at the same (0x60, 0xB0) through FUN_00410C71, which is what ties the hit rectangle to the picture.

functions.name: NetCmd_ReadMoveOrder
functions.comment: The receiving half of network command 0x29: reads player (1), a 4-byte value, unit (1), x (2), y (2) and journals sub-opcode 0x0C.
functions.basis: It sits between g_netCmdWriters[0x29] and g_netCmdWriters[0x2A] in address order, uses Net_ReadField where its neighbour used Net_WriteField, reads the same five widths in the same order, and passes the same sub-opcode 0x0C to Net_JournalCommand. The writer half IS verified and is in symbols.json.
functions.promotion: The reader is never called from the command table, so its caller has to be found - presumably a dispatch keyed on the received opcode byte. Naming that dispatcher promotes every reader at once.

functions.name: Net_ResolveDest
functions.comment: Turns 0x00544094 into the 4-byte value NetCmd_WriteMoveOrder puts second in the packet, ahead of the unit index.
functions.basis: Position in the payload only. Not read.

functions.name: Net_JournalCommand
functions.comment: Records an executed deterministic command into a ring of 0x38-byte slots at 0x0050D7C0: a live flag, the sub-opcode, and twelve int arguments. Both the writer and the reader of every command opcode call it, so it sees each command exactly once per peer.
functions.basis: Read in full. The slot layout is unambiguous - 0x0050D7C6 flag, 0x0050D7C7 sub-opcode, 0x0050D7C0 + 4*n arguments, stride 0x38. Every command writer/reader pair traced so far ends in a call to it. What is inferred is the PURPOSE: 'journal' rather than 'apply'. Nothing in the function itself changes game state.
functions.promotion: Find the consumer of the 0x0050D7C0 ring. If it replays the slots, this is a journal; if it is only a debug overlay, the name is wrong. Either answer is a check that could fail.

functions.name: Move_DistanceAcrossExpensive
functions.comment: Map_HoverUnitTarget uses it instead of the raw distance field whenever that field reads 100 or more, then adds 1. 100 is the cost the cost map gives an impassable-in-practice tile - castle, settlement, dwelling plot - so this looks like 'what would the cost be if the last step onto the objective were free'.
functions.basis: The call site and the 99 threshold, which matches Move_BuildCostMap's 100 exactly. The function body was not read.
functions.promotion: Read it, and check the result against a hand-computed path onto a county town in the England fixture.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateEngineWalk
functions.comment: Steps a siege engine along its route. Zeroes the figure aim point on the way out, as every non-firing engine state does.
functions.basis: slot 10 of g_manStateTable (0x004D9170), read out of the file
functions.caveat: The slot index is a fact; the name is a reading of a 184-byte body. It plays Anim_EngineMove, calls BattleMan_Step, and on stepFlags bit 1 - "was interrupted" - drops to state 11. Nothing outside the table says "engine", only that its animation helper is the one the four siege troop types use.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateEngineHalt
functions.comment: A siege engine standing still. BattleMan_StateChase sends any figure of troop type > 6 here rather than letting it pursue.
functions.basis: slot 11 of g_manStateTable; the state BattleMan_StateEngineWalk and BattleMan_StateChase both jump to
functions.caveat: A 62-byte body that plays the engine hold pose and zeroes the aim point, nothing more. "Halt" is the only thing it does; whether the original thought of it as halted, parked or arrived is not recoverable.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateEngineWork
functions.comment: Plays Anim_EngineWork and returns.
functions.basis: slot 13 of g_manStateTable
functions.caveat: A sixteen-byte thunk to the engine working animation and nothing else, so the body constrains the name almost not at all. It is the only state that plays that animation without also doing something.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateUnused16
functions.comment: Empty stub.
functions.basis: slot 16 of g_manStateTable
functions.caveat: An empty `ret`, like slot 0. Whether slot 16 is reachable was not checked; no writer of state = 16 was found by grep over the struct-typed corpus, but a computed write would not show up in that search.

functions.name: Bridge_Cross
functions.comment: Called from Cell_TryEnter for an attacking figure entering a bridge cell, with the cell x and y.
functions.basis: Cell_TryEnter calls it, and only when the cell surface is 7 and the figure side is 4
functions.caveat: battle.md 3 has surface 7 as bridge on independent evidence, and side 4 is the attacker. What the function then does to the bridge was not read.

functions.name: Anim_EngineMove
functions.comment: Siege-engine frames. Type 10 (oil) steps animPhase to 0x2F and reads frame 0x23 + phase >> 3; type 8 (tower) folds dirc and polarDirc into four half-facings; type 7 (catapult) uses dirc + 5 and a horse frame of dirc * 5.
functions.basis: the else-branch every a2 animation handler takes for troopType > 6
functions.caveat: The four branches are on troop types 7, 8, 9 and 10 and it writes frame and horseFrame, so it is certainly the siege-engine animation. "Move" versus "work" for this one and Anim_EngineWork rests only on which states call which.

functions.name: Anim_EngineHold
functions.comment: The still pose for a siege engine.
functions.basis: the third engine helper; every a2 handler that is not Anim_EngineMove falls back to it
functions.caveat: Called by thirteen functions and does the least of the three. "Hold" is a guess at intent.

functions.name: Anim_EngineWork
functions.comment: Siege-engine frames while the engine is doing its job. Reads g_horseWalkCycle.
functions.basis: the sibling of Anim_EngineMove; called by the firing and dying engine states
functions.caveat: Same shape as Anim_EngineMove with a longer animPhase range (0xA0 up for a catapult once swingTimer passes 100, 0x8F down for a ram) and the horse cycle table. That the longer animation is the working one is inference from the callers.

fields.name: merchantFlag
fields.basis: County_RecountMerchants zeroes it alongside +0x1A4 and +0x1A5, the two merchant fields.
fields.caveat: Zero in every county of every fixture, and nothing else in the corpus writes it, so the zeroing is all the evidence there is. It sits immediately before rationAchieved (+0x15D), so a width error here would be visible; it is a byte. Refuted if a writer turns up outside the merchant code.

fields.name: armyFoodSoldiers
fields.basis: The pair with +0x19C: Ration_Apply adds +0x198 + +0x19C to the food requirement when g_optArmiesEat is on. The evidence is written out on +0x19C.
fields.caveat: Shares the caveat of +0x19C: which of the two is soldiers and which is foragers is a coin flip off a dead string group, and both are 0 in every fixture.

fields.name: armyFoodForagers
fields.basis: Ration_Apply adds +0x198 + +0x19C to the county's food requirement when g_optArmiesEat is on, and Panel_Ration draws that same sum against L2.eng 87/8 'men foraging in the county.'. The orphaned ration group 62 has 'Soldiers', 'Foragers', 'take' and 'steal' as four separate strings, which is where the split into two fields comes from.
fields.caveat: That the pair exists and sums into the food bill is certain. Which of the two is soldiers and which is foragers is a guess off the dead string group, and is a coin flip. Both are 0 in every fixture - no fixture has an army standing in a county with Armies Eat on.

fields.name: purse
fields.basis: Three unrelated writers all treat it as money belonging to a county with no lord: Merchant_Trade credits and debits it instead of realm gold whenever the realm argument is 0, the tax pass banks an unowned county's taxCollected into it (FUN_0044B4F3), and the AI grants an unowned county a flat 100 a season (FUN_004A15xx). Ai_BuyGood then tests it as the purse for every unowned county's trade.
fields.caveat: Still 0 in every fixture, because no unowned county in any saved position has traded yet - so nothing has ever OBSERVED a non-zero value, only code that would produce one. crates/l2-kingdom's trade module exercises it and l2-game can now produce it, but our own engine agreeing with our own reading is not the check. Promote on a .sav taken after an AI season in which an unowned county traded: the offset should be non-zero and should equal tax banked plus grants minus purchases.

fields.name: farmStyle
fields.basis: Ai_ManageCountyFarms writes it from g_aiPersonality's farmStyle and immediately dispatches on 0, 1 and 9.
fields.caveat: Strong: the fixture holds only 0, 1 and 9, exactly the dispatched values. Left here rather than promoted because unowned counties also carry 1, and Ai_ManageCountyFarms only writes AI-owned ones, so something at map load writes it too and has not been found. The name may be too narrow.

fields.name: fieldsOther
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphics 0, 23 and 24 here, next to the three named field tallies.
fields.caveat: Zero in all fourteen counties of the England fixture, so the reproduction that verified the other four tallies could not verify this one - a bucket that never fires is a bucket whose meaning is unknown. Graphic 0 is an empty slot; 23 and 24 are not identified. Needs a save with those tiles.

fields.name: fieldsReclaimable
fields.basis: County_RecountFields buckets tile graphic 25 and above here; Field_SetType switches the reclamation labour share on exactly when it is non-zero.
fields.caveat: The gate in Field_SetType is direct and strong - this counts land the county can reclaim. What is not checked is the graphic band: it is 0 in every fixture, so no save demonstrates which tiles land in it. Promote when a save with wasteland exists.

globals.name: g_fileListTop
globals.basis: The only value SaveLoad_Scroll moves, by the widget's hotspot id, clamped at 0 and against DAT_004EB25C with a window of 15 rows for list 1 and 5 for list 2.
globals.comment: First visible row of the save/load file list.

globals.name: g_fileListCount
globals.basis: The bound SaveLoad_Scroll clamps g_fileListTop against.
globals.comment: How many files the save/load list holds.

globals.name: g_moveOriginX
globals.comment: The tile a movement flood-fill was seeded from. Move_ResetSelection writes it and its Y twin at 0x00504024, plus the flat index at 0x004F4070.
globals.basis: One writer, read in full. No reader traced.
globals.promotion: Find a reader - most likely Move_ExtractPath's terminator or the panel that prints a distance.

globals.name: g_netCmdJournal
globals.comment: Ring of 0x38-byte records Net_JournalCommand fills: +6 live flag, +7 sub-opcode, +0 and +4.. twelve int arguments.
globals.basis: The write pattern in Net_JournalCommand, which is unambiguous about the layout and silent about the purpose.

globals.name: g_garrisonPendingCounty
globals.comment: The county Army_Garrison stashes for Army_GarrisonConfirm, alongside the unit at 0x0055CD58. The address sits 8 bytes BELOW g_units (0x0052F0B0), so it is not part of any unit record.
globals.basis: Two sites, matched writer and reader. That is all.
globals.promotion: Check no third site writes it.

globals.name: g_moveOrderDest
globals.comment: Whatever NetCmd_WriteMoveOrder passes to Net_ResolveDest to make the packet's second field.
globals.basis: One call site. Nothing else traced reads it.

globals.name: g_rampartCellsBreached
globals.comment: How many rampart cells this siege has knocked through.
globals.basis: incremented beside g_wallHitsRampart every time a rampart cell is converted to surface 4
globals.caveat: The mechanism is read; the name is a guess at what the count is for. BattleMan_StateRamGate reads it back and sends the figure to state 11 once it passes 1.

globals.name: g_playerSlots
globals.basis: Mp_DropDepartedPlayers tests slot +0x00 for zero; Realm_Eliminate clears +0x00, +0x25, +0x26 and sets +0x27. Stride 0x2C, six entries, one per realm.
globals.caveat: A per-realm table whose first word means 'this realm is still attached' is the only reading that makes both functions work. What the table actually holds - a network peer, a save slot, a controller - is not established, and the name presumes the first.

globals.name: g_playerCount
globals.basis: Decremented by Mp_DropDepartedPlayers each time a realm is dropped.
globals.caveat: One writer, one direction. Nothing here shows what increments it or who reads it.

globals.name: g_gateBreached
globals.comment: Set once when the 20000-hit accumulator breaches; also raises g_siegeApproachScore and g_siegeBreachScore by 4.
globals.basis: set to 1 exactly once, at the 20000-hit threshold in both wall-attack states
globals.caveat: A one-shot flag on the gate/wall threshold, read by BattleUnit_FewOnRampart and UnitOrder_SiegeAttRam. "Gate" rather than "wall" is inference from its being the non-rampart branch.

globals.name: g_tradeGood
globals.basis: Indexes g_merchantStall in the trade panel and selects the branch in the good-to-stock switch.
globals.caveat: Consistent everywhere it appears. Not promoted because the trade screen was not read end to end here - only the transaction underneath it.

corrections.claim: UNRESOLVED, and flagged rather than explained. The bow-draw animation is the only function in the battle that reads g_mapRotation - the campaign map orientation, 0/2/4/6 - and it rotates the figure facing by it before choosing a frame.
evidence: Nothing else in the battle reads it: not the terrain renderer, not BattleFigure_Draw, not the other five animation handlers.
docs/battle.md 13.1 has the battlefield as a plain top-down grid with no rotation.
The identical idiom appears in the campaign unit renderer at 0x00400000+0x4508, facing minus g_mapRotation.
corrections.notDoneBecause: Either the battlefield honours a rotation nothing else implements, or this is a paste from the campaign renderer whose three extra branches never run. Both stories are coherent and neither is anchored. Deciding it needs a live battle or the 16-pixel renderer read.

corrections.claim: The doc comment named a field that does not exist. Figure +0x144/+0x146 fall inside the 300-byte path array at +0x38, no instruction in the binary references either offset, and the field is tg x / tg y at +0x24/+0x26. "Written by Formation_SendFigure and by nothing else" is also wrong: eleven functions write it.
evidence: docs/records.json gives BattleMan +0x38 as u8[300], which runs to +0x164.

Grep over the struct-typed corpus finds .tgX = or .tgY = in BattleMan_Create, BattleMan_StateChase, BattleMan_StateEngineFire, BattleMan_StateCloseToAttack, Formation_SendFigure, BattleMan_Step, and five functions at 0x004923A8, 0x0049260E, 0x004926FB, 0x004927FA and 0x00492951.
corrections.notDoneBecause: Fixed in place by this pass. Recorded because the field is still untested.

corrections.claim: The walking and attacking blocks are the other way round. Frames 0..5 of a facing block are the WALK cycle and 6..N-2 are the strike; N-1 is the standing pose.
evidence: Anim_WalkA2 (0x00486D83) computes dirc * N + (animPhase >> 2) with the phase wrapping at 0x17 - poses 0..5 - and is called at the top of BattleMan_StateWalk and BattleMan_StateChase.
Anim_StrikeA2 (0x00486249) computes dirc2 * N + 6 + cycle[...] and is called at the top of BattleMan_StateMelee and BattleMan_StateAttackWall.
BattleMan_StateMelee calls Anim_WalkA2 only when BattleMan_Step actually moved the figure; BattleMan_StateWalk calls Anim_StandA2 when it did not.
Anim_StrikeA2 plays the cycle only while the figure holds the attacker role (+0x185 == 1) and otherwise shows the standing pose - the melee defender stands while the attacker swings.

The block sizes close: peasants N=10, walk 0..5, strike 6..8 from a cycle whose maximum is 2, stand 9. Macemen N=12, strike 6..10 from a cycle whose maximum is 4, stand 11. Crossbowmen and archers N=13, strike 6..8, stand 9, and 10..12 are the bow draw, which is where Anim_DrawBowA2 gets its +10.
corrections.notDoneBecause: Corrected in place in docs/battle.md 13.5 and 13.8 by this pass. Recorded here because crates/l2-view may encode the old reading.

corrections.claim: State 6 is not "blocked" and state 9 is not "siege-wall movement". State 6 is a figure attacking the castle wall it just walked into; state 9 is the moat fill.
evidence: g_manStateTable slot 6 is 0x00483A88, which accumulates wall damage and converts rampart cells to surface 4.
A figure reaches it from BattleMan_Step when BattleMan_TryStepDir returns 5, which Cell_TryEnter returns only for cell flag 0x20 against a non-zero side - already [V] in docs/battle.md 3.
Slot 9 is 0x00483FE1, which reads g_moatFillSteps; docs/battle-ai.md 5 already describes state 9 as the moat fill.
corrections.notDoneBecause: Corrected in place in docs/battle.md 2.2 by this pass.

corrections.claim: Something in the County record between +0x290 and +0x2F3 is laid out wrong. The county strip reads commodity c at +0x2A8 + c*0x18, and under the current layout — Industry[4] at +0x290, stride 0x18 — that expression is Industry[c+1] + 0x00, an unnamed head word, and for c = 3 it is +0x2F0, one whole record past the end of a four-record array. One of the base, the stride, the count or the field set is wrong, and this correction does NOT say which.
evidence: The corpus has byte reads at county +0x2A8 and +0x2F0, both guarded `!= 0` and both copied into a panel buffer (00450000.c:7436, 8382, 4044) — 0x2F0 - 0x2A8 = 0x48 = 3 * 0x18, so they are element 0 and element 3 of one 0x18-strided run beginning at +0x2A8.
docs/records.json places Industry[4] at +0x290 with size 24, so the array occupies +0x290..+0x2EF and +0x2A8 is Industry[1] + 0x00.
County.levySurcharge is at +0x2F4, so the array cannot simply have a fifth element: Industry[4] would span +0x2F0..+0x307 and swallow it.
Industry's first named field is `efficiency` at +0x04, so offset +0x00 of the record is unnamed in the current layout — which is why nothing has noticed.
corrections.notDoneBecause: records.json is applied to the Ghidra database by ApplyRecords.java, so a wrong record layout propagates into every function in the corpus that touches a county — which is correction C3 exactly. Settling it needs CountyStrip_Draw and Industry_Produce read against the binary to say whether the base, the stride or the field set is wrong, and an integrator picking one of those on the balance of probability is how a plausible wrong layout gets written down as fact. The peasant-interaction pass found it, left the strip's right-hand column a labelled stub rather than a guess, and said so; this entry is the hand-off rather than a repair.

claims.subject: The raised county defence never gets a moveAllowance or a sprite because Army_Tick has not run on it yet
claims.comment: battle-during.sav slot 6 is a defence raised the same turn and carries moveAllowance 0 AND spriteFrame 0, while the two ordinary armies in the same save carry 15 and a correct sprite. Army_Tick writes both unconditionally at the top of every tick. So 'moveAllowance is 15 for an army' (docs/armies.md section 1.2) is a tick-maintained invariant, not an initial value, and a freshly created army is briefly outside it.
claims.basis: Three unit records in one fixture, plus Army_Tick read in full. Two of three agree and the third disagrees in exactly the way the explanation predicts.
claims.promotion: A fixture in which a defence survives into a following turn: it should then read 15. Nothing available today can produce one.

claims.subject: Unit +0x07 lags +0x1B by one walk phase
claims.comment: battle-during.sav slot 5 has facing 2, walkPhase 0 and spriteFrame 82, where Army_Tick's formula gives 0x48 + 3*((2+1)&7) + g_unitWalkFrames[0] = 81. The other two armies match exactly. Army_Tick writes +0x07 and then calls Unit_Step, which advances +0x1B - so the saved sprite is one phase behind the saved phase, and 82 - 81 = 1 is a value the table actually contains.
claims.basis: Three records; the discrepancy is exactly one walk-frame unit and the ordering in Army_Tick explains it. This is a reading that fits, which is why it is here and not in symbols.json.
claims.promotion: Read Unit_Step's +0x1B update and confirm it runs after the sprite write on the path that produced this record. If it does not, the formula or the table is wrong instead.

claims.subject: Map_Click's fifth industry rung, record 4 for castle graphics
claims.comment: Map_Click maps a clicked building's graphic to an industry record: below 4 -> 1, below 7 -> 3, below 10 -> 2, below 0x0D -> 0, and 0x15 or above -> 4. The first four rungs agree exactly with Unit_TrampleTile's ruin ladder and County_PlaceResourceSites' placement, a three-way agreement. The fifth has no counterpart in either, and docs/armies.md section 3.5 lists only records 0..3.
claims.basis: One function. The other two functions are silent about record 4 rather than contradicting it.
claims.promotion: Find a fifth industry record in the county layout, or a second reader of index 4. Silence from two functions is not evidence for it.

claims.subject: MoveOrder_ConfirmGarrison offers to split an army that will not fit
claims.comment: When the castle's remaining capacity is below the incoming army's men, the callback sends message 0xA6 with the unit, the county and a fourth value, and L2.eng group 166 carries 'Your army contains' / 'more troops can be stationed here.' / 'Do you want to split your army?' beside its 'Cannot garrison castle.' heading. Nothing in the knowledge base records an army-splitting mechanic.
claims.basis: The strings are certain. That message 0xA6 leads to a working split, rather than to a prompt whose yes-branch does something else, is not.
claims.promotion: Find message 0xA6's handler and read what its yes-branch does to the two unit records.

claims.subject: County_RaiseDefence's mode-1 auto-equip moves men ten at a time
claims.comment: The AI branch loops at most 50 times over the six weapon slots, moving 10 men from the realm's stock into each slot per pass and stopping when the remaining headcount drops below 10. So an AI county's defence is equipped in blocks of ten, round-robin by weapon type, and the last nine men are always peasants.
claims.basis: The loop read in full. Never observed - the fixture's only raised defence is a neutral county on the mode-2 path, whose ladder IS verified.
claims.promotion: A save with a defence raised in an AI-owned county. The signature is a troop count divisible by 10 in every equipped slot.

claims.subject: Giving a besieging army a move order is the only routine way to lift a siege
claims.comment: Siege_Break has three callers: Unit_OrderMove on a successful type-1 order, Siege_LaunchAssault refusing for want of engines, and the siege screen's own button. Siege_ValidateLink can also clear +0x199, but only when the garrison side of the link has already gone.
claims.basis: An exhaustive grep of the writes to +0x199 across the whole corpus, which is mechanical. What is inferred is that the set is complete in the sense that matters - the corpus is decompiled C and an indirect write through a struct pointer would not be found by that grep.
claims.promotion: Nothing cheap. Recorded so that a later reader knows the grep was by field name, not by address.
